about: Peer-reviewed trial papers that say what a drug binds and how it did in UC (added 2026-11-26 after an expert-style review of the top candidates). Each quote is copied verbatim from the PubMed abstract; drug_literature.py checks this against PubMed when online. Genes: the genes whose statements may cite the record.

records.title: Ustekinumab as Induction and Maintenance Therapy for Ulcerative Colitis.
records.binds: p40 (IL12B), shared by IL-12 and IL-23
quotes: The efficacy of ustekinumab, an antagonist of the p40 subunit of interleukin-12 and interleukin-23, as induction and maintenance therapy in patients with ulcerative colitis is unknown.
Ustekinumab was more effective than placebo for inducing and maintaining remission in patients with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.

records.title: Mirikizumab as Induction and Maintenance Therapy for Ulcerative Colitis.
quotes: Mirikizumab, a p19-directed antibody against interleukin-23, showed efficacy in the treatment of ulcerative colitis in a phase 2 trial.
Mirikizumab was more effective than placebo in inducing and maintaining clinical remission in patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.

records.title: Tofacitinib as Induction and Maintenance Therapy for Ulcerative Colitis.
quotes: Tofacitinib, an oral, small-molecule Janus kinase inhibitor, was shown to have potential efficacy as induction therapy for ulcerative colitis in a phase 2 trial.
In patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis, tofacitinib was more effective as induction and maintenance therapy than placebo.

records.title: Upadacitinib as induction and maintenance therapy for moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis: results from three phase 3, multicentre, double-blind, randomised trials.
quotes: We assessed the efficacy and safety of upadacitinib, an oral selective Janus kinase 1 inhibitor, as induction and maintenance therapy in patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.
Upadacitinib demonstrated a positive efficacy and safety profile and could be an effective treatment option for patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.

records.title: Filgotinib as induction and maintenance therapy for ulcerative colitis (SELECTION): a phase 2b/3 double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
quotes: We assessed the efficacy and safety of filgotinib, a once-daily, oral Janus kinase 1 preferential inhibitor, for treatment of ulcerative colitis.
Filgotinib 200 mg was well tolerated, and efficacious in inducing and maintaining clinical remission compared with placebo in patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.

records.journal: Am J Respir Crit Care Med
records.title: CXCR2 Antagonist MK-7123. A Phase 2 Proof-of-Concept Trial for Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
quotes: MK-7123 caused a dose-dependent decrease in absolute neutrophil count (ANC) and reduced inflammatory biomarkers matrix metallopeptidase-9 and myeloperoxidase in plasma and sputum; ANC lower than 1.5 × 10(9)/L led to discontinuations with higher doses of MK-7123 (18% in the MK-7123 50-mg group vs. 1% in placebo).
Rates of infections at 6 months were similar in all groups.

records.title: SB-656933, a novel CXCR2 selective antagonist, inhibits ex vivo neutrophil activation and ozone-induced airway inflammation in humans.
quotes: SB-656933 is a CXCR2 antagonist that demonstrates dose-dependent effects on neutrophil activation and recruitment within a well-tolerated dose range.

records.title: Risankizumab for Ulcerative Colitis: Two Randomized Clinical Trials.
quotes: The clinical effects of risankizumab (a monoclonal antibody that selectively targets the p19 subunit of IL-23) for the treatment of ulcerative colitis are unknown.
Compared with placebo, risankizumab improved clinical remission rates in an induction trial and in a maintenance trial for patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.

records.title: Guselkumab in patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (QUASAR): phase 3 double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled induction and maintenance studies.
quotes: Guselkumab is a dual-acting, human IgG1, interleukin-23p19 subunit inhibitor that potently neutralises interleukin-23 and can bind to CD64.
Guselkumab was effective and safe as induction and maintenance therapy in patients with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.

records.title: Deucravacitinib in patients with inflammatory bowel disease: 12-week efficacy and safety results from 3 randomized phase 2 studies in Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
quotes: Tyrosine kinase 2 is a downstream intracellular mediator of interleukin-23 signaling, which has a key role in the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease.
Deucravacitinib at multiple doses did not demonstrate significant clinical benefit vs placebo in moderately to severely active Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis.

records.title: JAK selectivity and the implications for clinical inhibition of pharmacodynamic cytokine signalling by filgotinib, upadacitinib, tofacitinib and baricitinib.
records.trial: pharmacology in human blood and phase 1 volunteers
records.binds: JAK1 pathways most potently; filgotinib least on JAK2- and JAK3-dependent pathways
quotes: JAK1-dependent pathways (interferon (IFN)α/pSTAT5, interleukin (IL)-6/pSTAT1) were among the most potently inhibited by all JAKinibs in healthy and RA blood, with filgotinib exhibiting the greatest selectivity for JAK1 pathways.

Filgotinib inhibited JAK1-mediated signalling similarly to other JAKinibs, but with less inhibition of JAK2-dependent and JAK3-dependent pathways, providing a mechanistic rationale for its apparently differentiated efficacy:safety profile.

records.title: Oral Ritlecitinib and Brepocitinib for Moderate-to-Severe Ulcerative Colitis: Results From a Randomized, Phase 2b Study.
quotes: The efficacy and safety of ritlecitinib (oral JAK3/TEC family kinase inhibitor) and brepocitinib (oral TYK2/JAK1 inhibitor) as induction therapy were assessed in patients with active, moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.
Ritlecitinib and brepocitinib induction therapies were more effective than placebo for the treatment of moderate-to-severe active ulcerative colitis, with an acceptable short-term safety profile.

tags.IL12B: UC: ustekinumab binds it (p40); anti-p19 mirikizumab, risankizumab, guselkumab bind IL23A
tags.IL23A: UC: anti-p19 mirikizumab, risankizumab, guselkumab bind it; ustekinumab binds IL12B (p40)
tags.JAK2: UC: tofacitinib (JAK inhibitor, more JAK2/JAK3-pathway inhibition than filgotinib); upadacitinib, filgotinib (JAK1-selective or -preferential)
tags.TYK2: UC phase 2: TYK2-selective deucravacitinib failed; TYK2/JAK1 brepocitinib effective
tags.CXCR2: UC: tested in phase 2, not advanced (SB-656933, navarixin); lowers blood neutrophils

synonyms.source: NLM MeSH supplementary concept C000730055 (navarixin); PubMed maps the terms 'SCH 527123' and 'MK-7123' to its chemical name
synonyms.sentence: navarixin (MeSH supplementary concept C000730055) is the compound also coded SCH-527123 and MK-7123: PubMed maps both codes to its chemical name, 2-hydroxy-N,N-dimethyl-3-((2-(((1R)-1-(5-methylfuran-2-yl)propyl)amino)-3,4-dioxocyclobuten-1-yl)amino)benzamide.
